bibl.title: Opening Holes in the Blanket of Inhibition: Localized Lateral Disinhibition by VIP Interneurons

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the spatial extent over which a single VIP interneuron disinhibits the surrounding cortical network
span.quote: However, little is known about the fine structure of PC disinhibition through the VIP→SOM→PC circuit, although recent evidence suggests a spatially restricted mode of action for this circuit that may be related to “the spotlight of attention” ( Zhang et al., 2014 ). This facilitation of visual responses is enhanced during locomotion ( Fu et al., 2014 ). Reconstructions of VIPs show many double bouquet-like axons ( Kawaguchi and Kubota, 1996 ; Bayraktar et al., 2000 ; Tahvildari et al., 2012 ; Lee et al., 2013 ), consistent with horizontally local output. However, individual neuron activation experiments necessary to directly measure the spatial extent of disinhibition mediated by a VIP cell have not been performed.

span.label: how excitatory activity can propagate at all through a cortex covered by blanket inhibition
span.quote: Inhibitory interneurons in the neocortex often connect in a promiscuous and extensive fashion, extending a “blanket of inhibition” on the circuit. This raises the problem of how can excitatory activity propagate in the midst of this widespread inhibition.

span.label: measures the disinhibitory reach of a single VIP cell by four independent methods and converges on about 120 microns, giving the blanket-of-inhibition problem a quantitative answer
span.quote: Although our in vitro results may be underestimates due to the inevitability of cut processes in brain slices, the similarity of the in vivo results increases their credibility, and together the data suggest a ∼120 μm lateral radius of effect for single VIPs.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: The data in Figure 1 indicate that VIPs specialize in lateral disinhibition and can block FDDI by inhibiting SOMs.

span.label: localized lateral disinhibition by VIP interneurons
span.quote: Our data indicate that VIPs can make ∼240 μm diameter holes in the blanket of inhibition mediated by SOMs ( Fino and Yuste, 2011 ; Karnani et al., 2014 ).

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: In this study, we show with intracellular recordings and optogenetics in neocortical layer 2/3 that VIP activation can override lateral disynaptic inhibition between PCs in slices.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A VIP cell inhibits nearby SOM cells, which removes the SOM-mediated blanket inhibition on local pyramidal cells and thereby lets excitation spread through that patch.
span.quote: The data in Figure 1 indicate that VIPs specialize in lateral disinhibition and can block FDDI by inhibiting SOMs.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The horizontally narrow VIP axon confines the disinhibitory action to a small cylindrical volume of cortex, setting the size of the hole.
span.quote: A horizontally narrow axon ( Fig. 2 A–D ) may restrict the area of effect of a single VIP to a small cylindrical volume of cortex.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: During locomotion many VIPs are recruited at once, so the disinhibition from any single stimulated VIP is swamped and loses its spatial structure.
span.quote: This is likely because of the increased neuronal activity and recruitment of many more VIPs than the stimulated one during locomotion.

span.label: the problem: SOM, PV and chandelier cells inhibit most or all pyramidal cells within their axonal arbors, which in principle should stop excitation propagating at all
span.quote: Members of the SOM, PV, and chandelier cell populations mediate a broad blanket-like inhibition of most if not all PCs within their axonal arbors ( Fino and Yuste, 2011 ; Packer and Yuste, 2011 ; Karnani et al., 2014 ; Inan et al., 2013 ). This widespread inhibition, in principle, should suppress the propagation of excitatory activity in neocortex.

span.label: the interneuron population looks designed to block both fast and slow excitatory activity, since PV and SOM are driven by fast and slow inputs respectively
span.quote: In fact, because PV and SOM are activated specifically with fast and slow inputs, and relay fast and slow inhibition, it seems as if the interneuron population was selectively designed to block both fast and slow excitatory activity.

span.label: VIP cells inhibit nearby SOM cells, and SOM cells inhibit pyramidal cells, so activating one VIP opens a local hole in the inhibitory blanket
span.quote: We find that VIP interneurons have narrow axons and inhibit nearby somatostatin interneurons, which themselves inhibit pyramidal cells. Moreover, via this lateral disinhibition, VIP cells in vivo make local and transient “holes” in the inhibitory blanket extended by SOM cells.

span.label: two-photon spiral scanning excites one targeted VIP and not its neighbours, which is what makes single-cell activation possible
span.quote: Targeting the stimulation to other nearby VIPs did not excite the recorded VIP

span.label: the disinhibitory effect requires concurrent sensory drive - there must be activity for the hole to admit
span.quote: As the presence of sensory stimulation ( Fig. 6 ) was required for seeing the disinhibitory effect of single VIP activation (data not shown) the spatiotemporal coincidence of excitation and a disinhibitory hole may be necessary to use the hole in blanket inhibition.

span.label: two possible regimes: single VIPs opening tiny patches, or a few nearby VIPs together opening larger ones
span.quote: VIPs may be active individually, e.g., during low-activity states or a specific input from prefrontal cortex ( Harris and Thiele, 2011 ; Zhang et al., 2014 ). This mode of activity may thus form highly localized disinhibited patches of cortex. Alternatively, a few closely spaced VIPs may be preferentially activated together, thus forming larger patches of disinhibited cortex.

span.label: All recordings came from layer 2/3, so the conclusions do not necessarily hold for deeper layers.
span.quote: We note that as all our recordings were from layer 2/3, they only apply there, and it is possible that VIPs mediate qualitatively different effects in the deeper layers where some of them project axons ( Fig. 2 A ).

span.label: Slice measurements of spatial reach may underestimate the true extent because processes are cut.
span.quote: Although our in vitro results may be underestimates due to the inevitability of cut processes in brain slices, the similarity of the in vivo results increases their credibility, and together the data suggest a ∼120 μm lateral radius of effect for single VIPs.

span.label: The correlational in vivo data are directionally ambiguous: nearby cells could be driving the VIPs rather than the reverse.
span.quote: These results are consistent with VIPs disinhibiting a small nearby volume of cortex in vivo , during both spontaneous and visually evoked activity, but might equally arise from the nearby cells driving the VIPs.

span.label: all recordings are from layer 2/3 and the authors say the conclusions only apply there
span.quote: We note that as all our recordings were from layer 2/3, they only apply there, and it is possible that VIPs mediate qualitatively different effects in the deeper layers where some of them project axons ( Fig. 2 A ).

span.label: slice results may underestimate the reach because processes are cut
span.quote: Although our in vitro results may be underestimates due to the inevitability of cut processes in brain slices, the similarity of the in vivo results increases their credibility

span.label: the correlational results could equally reflect nearby cells driving the VIPs rather than the reverse, which is why the optogenetic experiment was needed
span.quote: These results are consistent with VIPs disinhibiting a small nearby volume of cortex in vivo , during both spontaneous and visually evoked activity, but might equally arise from the nearby cells driving the VIPs.

span.label: during locomotion the spatial structure disappears, attributed to many more VIPs being recruited
span.quote: However, during locomotion epochs the distance dependence was scrambled ( Fig. 7 C ). This is likely because of the increased neuronal activity and recruitment of many more VIPs than the stimulated one during locomotion.

span.label: six cells were inhibited rather than disinhibited and were set aside as under 1% of the sample
span.quote: Because the inhibited cells formed <1% of all cells, we did not analyze them further, though we note they may be SOMs based on their occurrence and inhibition by VIPs.

span.label: the requirement for sensory stimulation is supported by data not shown
span.quote: As the presence of sensory stimulation ( Fig. 6 ) was required for seeing the disinhibitory effect of single VIP activation (data not shown) the spatiotemporal coincidence of excitation and a disinhibitory hole may be necessary to use the hole in blanket inhibition.

span.label: the spotlight metaphor, imported as the functional interpretation of a local disinhibitory hole
span.quote: VIP interneurons, themselves regulated by neuromodulators, may therefore enable selective patterns of activity to propagate through the cortex, by generating a “spotlight of attention

span.label: attractors, offered as what selectively sculpted circuits might implement
span.quote: This type of local control could be use to dynamically sculpt selective cortical circuits out of a neural network type of connectivity matrix, and use them to implement specific perceptions, behaviors, memory states or, more generally, dynamical attractors.

span.label: blanket of inhibition is the specific claim that SOM, PV and chandelier cells inhibit most or all pyramidal cells within their arbors indiscriminately - it is what makes disinhibition necessary rather than merely available
span.quote: Members of the SOM, PV, and chandelier cell populations mediate a broad blanket-like inhibition of most if not all PCs within their axonal arbors ( Fino and Yuste, 2011 ; Packer and Yuste, 2011 ; Karnani et al., 2014 ; Inan et al., 2013 ). This widespread inhibition, in principle, should suppress the propagation of excitatory activity in neocortex.

span.label: the hole is measured four different ways - axon extent, paired connectivity, activity correlation, and single-cell optogenetics - and reported as a radius of about 120 microns, equivalently a diameter of about 240
span.quote: Our results indicate that morphologically VIP axons extend ∼233 μm/2 = 116 μm laterally, whereas functionally inhibiting SOMs within a reach of ∼112 μm ( Fig. 2 ; see Results); VIPs have increased correlation with cells ∼75–150 μm away laterally depending on the behavioral state of the animal ( Figs. 3 , 4 ); and when activated optogenetically, single VIPs can disinhibit cells within ∼60–120 μm depending on behavioral state ( Figs. 6 , 7 ).

span.label: spotlight of attention is used as an analogy for what a local disinhibitory hole could implement, not as a claim that it does
span.quote: VIP interneurons, themselves regulated by neuromodulators, may therefore enable selective patterns of activity to propagate through the cortex, by generating a “spotlight of attention

span.label: disinhibited is defined operationally as a visual response increasing by more than two standard deviations during VIP activation
span.quote: Across 27 experiments (pooled awake and anesthetized data), we classified cells as disinhibited (33/638 cells) if their visual responses increased >2 × SD during the VIP activation, as inhibited (6/638 cells) if they decreased >2 × SD, and as unchanged otherwise (599 cells).

span.label: extends → Kapfer et al. (2007), Silberberg and Markram (2007) and Murayama et al. (2009) on SOM-mediated frequency-dependent disynaptic inhibition
span.quote: While many experiments are consistent with SOMs mediating frequency-dependent disynaptic inhibition (FDDI) between neighboring PCs, a cell-type-specific loss-of-function experiment has not been performed ( Kapfer et al., 2007 ; Silberberg and Markram, 2007 ; Murayama et al., 2009 ).

span.label: replicates → Zhang et al. (2014) on the uniquely localized disinhibitory effect of VIP cells
span.quote: A recent report also concluded that VIPs, in contrast to SOMs and PVs, have a uniquely localized disinhibitory effect with a radius of <200 μm ( Zhang et al., 2014 ).

span.label: extends → Pi et al. 2013 and Fu et al. 2014 on the VIP to SOM disinhibitory motif - both independently tagged in this corpus
span.quote: Indeed, inhibitory connectivity among SOM, VIP, and PV populations has recently been shown to form specific disinhibitory motifs, most importantly through the inhibitory connection from VIPs to SOMs

span.label: supports → Zhang et al., who also found VIPs uniquely localised with a radius under 200 microns
span.quote: A recent report also concluded that VIPs, in contrast to SOMs and PVs, have a uniquely localized disinhibitory effect with a radius of <200

span.label: supports → morphological reports that VIP axons are horizontally restricted
span.quote: Our results indicate that morphologically VIP axons extend ∼233 μm/2 = 116 μm laterally, whereas functionally inhibiting SOMs within a reach of ∼112 μm ( Fig. 2 ; see Results); VIPs have increased correlation with cells ∼75–150 μm away laterally depending on the behavioral state of the animal ( Figs. 3 , 4 ); and when activated optogenetically, single VIPs can disinhibit cells within ∼60–120 μm depending on behavioral state ( Figs. 6 , 7 ).

span.label: extends → Fu et al. 2014 on locomotion driving VIP activity, by showing the spatial structure is lost in that state
span.quote: However, during locomotion epochs the distance dependence was scrambled ( Fig. 7 C ). This is likely because of the increased neuronal activity and recruitment of many more VIPs than the stimulated one during locomotion.

span.label: VIP —causes→ SOM
span.note: inhibits. same edge as Fu2014 and Pi2013 - three corpus papers now carry it, from three labs
span.quote: We find that VIP interneurons have narrow axons and inhibit nearby somatostatin interneurons, which themselves inhibit pyramidal cells. Moreover, via this lateral disinhibition, VIP cells in vivo make local and transient “holes” in the inhibitory blanket extended by SOM cells.

span.quote: We find that VIP interneurons have narrow axons and inhibit nearby somatostatin interneurons, which themselves inhibit pyramidal cells. Moreover, via this lateral disinhibition, VIP cells in vivo make local and transient “holes” in the inhibitory blanket extended by SOM cells.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · SOM —operationalised-as→ lateral inhibition
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span named the SOM population without naming lateral inhibition. This sentence names both and states the mechanism - lateral inhibition 'is thought to WORK THROUGH somatostatin-expressing INs (SOMs)'. It also fixes a Q-267 defect in passing: the old span attested `SOM` only inside `somatostatin`.

This widespread inhibition, in principle, should suppress the propagation of excitatory activity in neocortex.

span.note: RE-GROUNDS Karnani2016-opening-holes-in-the-blanket-of-inhibition-l[2]: the old span named ONE endpoint.
span.quote: In the rodent neocortex disynaptic lateral inhibition between nearby pyramidal cells (PCs) is thought to work through somatostatin-expressing INs (SOMs; Kapfer et al., 2007 ; Silberberg and Markram, 2007 ; Adesnik et al., 2012 ).

span.quote: However, when we exposed the slice to green light during this time to inhibit SOMs, the disynaptic inhibition was blocked, confirming that SOMs mediate FDDI ( Fig. 1 D–G ).

span.label: Spontaneous VIP activity in awake mice was tied to activity of cells within about 50 μm, whereas pyramidal-cell activity showed almost no such distance dependence.
span.quote: This analysis showed that spontaneous activity in VIPs is closely tied to activity in the other cells within a 50 μm radius, whereas activity in PCs showed a weak distance dependence with nearby cells ( Fig. 3 E ).
